Cornish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From lader (“thief”) +‎ -a.

Verb

[edit]

ladra

  1. to rob, steal, thieve

Conjugation

[edit]

[edit]

Galician

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈlaðɾɐ]

Noun

[edit]

ladra f (plural ladras)

  1. female equivalent of ladrón (“robber, thief”)
  2. a roguish sheep
  3. common wall gecko (Tarentola mauritanica)
    Synonyms: lasca, osga

References

[edit]
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, editor (2006–2013), “ladra”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios da lingua galega [Dictionary of Dictionaries of the Galician language] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, Ernesto Xosé González Seoane, María Álvarez de la Granja, editors (2003–2018), “ladra”, in Tesouro informatizado da lingua galega (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Rosario Álvarez Blanco, editor (2014–2024), “ladra”, in Tesouro do léxico patrimonial galego e portugués (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega, →ISSN

Etymology 2

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

ladra

  1. inflection of ladrar:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈla.dra/
  • Rhymes: -adra
  • Hyphenation: là‧dra

Noun

[edit]

ladra f (plural ladre)

Adjective

ladra

Polish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

(This etymology is missing or incomplete. Please add to it, or discuss it at the Etymology scriptorium.)

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Masovia):
    • (Near Masovian) IPA(key): [ˈla.dra]
  • (Lesser Poland):
    • (Kielce) IPA(key): [ˈla.dra]

Noun

[edit]

ladra f

  1. (Kielce) straw chute (part of a chaff cutter where straw is placed)
  2. (Near Masovian, Łuków County) counter (box next to a forage harvester)

Further reading

[edit]
